items.title: If it was that simple, we’d already have a 5 trillion model.
items.summary:
If it was that simple, we’d already have a 5 trillion model.

Unfortunately there are limits to the available data and what can be trained into the model. We hit that wall sometime around GPT 4. The scaling phase of LLMs has ended and the quality density phase has begun.

With that said, I don’t think we’ll ever see LLMs writing better code than humans. Regurgitating patterns of code written by others isn’t a very scalable solution, and it can’t exceed the capabilities or quality baked into the training data.

items.title: AI data centers took a beating in the midterm elections. A reckoning may be ahead for tech giants - The Dispatch
items.summary:
AI giant OpenAI published a framework Thursday enumerating new commitments to the communities where it develops data centers. The company said it was asking federal, state and local policymakers to write “clear rules for how the industry builds.”

“Lawmakers should establish rules to advance responsible investment, protect residents, and ensure that the benefits of AI infrastructure are broadly shared,” the post said. [...] On Thursday, the Nasdaq, which is full of AI-related and other tech stocks, sank 11% below its all-time high amid worries that data center construction may slow because it’s getting costlier to borrow money.

AI data center construction is driving much of the U.S. economy’s growth, and any slowdown could have a broader chilling effect. [...] HARRISBURG, Pa. — After a campaign season filled with outrage against artificial intelligence data centers, the midterm elections ushered in a wave of Democrats pledging to clamp down on the energy-hungry behemoths.

A tougher regulatory environment for AI giants and data center developers is expected to follow, even if President Donald Trump — perhaps the industry’s biggest champion — stalls any federal crackdown.

items.title: Recent advances in AI are creating a 'paradigm shift' for robotics - Berkeley News
items.summary:
Traditionally, engineers can directly program the software that tells robots how to perceive objects, plan movements and control their actions, a process called model-based robotics. Or, with model-free robotics, they can train robots to learn behaviors from demonstrations through imitation learning. The first approach requires extensive engineering, while the second needs enormous amounts of data and time. [...] Berkeley-based Ambi Robotics, which specializes in logistics and warehouse order fulfillment, applied the new methods earlier this year to analyze parcel sorting data and test updates to robot behavior. Tests showed an increased capacity of over 15,000 packages sorted annually per robot; the change is now deployed across 30% of the company’s U.S. fleet. [...] Ken Goldberg

“Agentic robotics is a fundamental shift in how robots are controlled,” Goldberg said. “Instead of collecting massive amounts of data and hand-tuning every behavior, teams of agents can quickly generate, test and refine robot programs that allow human engineers to interpret how the programs work for fine-tuning and verification.”

https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.title: Anthropic and OpenAI are coming for the development workflow | InfoWorld
items.summary: This is clearly where the frontier labs are moving, even though they’ve all benefited from an industry that provided neutral spaces to build. For example, OpenAI developed Pando, a Git back end for its own monorepo, to handle more engineers and agents reading and writing code concurrently. Its engineers kept using Git. OpenAI retained compatibility with the protocol and client and contributed improvements upstream. That compatibility let it rebuild the back end around the way its engineers [...] This pressure to maximize profitability helps explain why frontier labs like Anthropic and OpenAI are aggressively adding functionality to own more of the developer’s workflow. On November 4, OpenAI announced an agreement to buy Pierre, the company behind Code Storage and the open source libraries Codex already uses to browse files and review changes. OpenAI wants Codex to be where developers work, from the first branch an agent creates through deployment of the application. There’s money in [...] OpenAI or Anthropic could build the place developers prefer to work. The question is what happens when a team likes that place and wants a rival’s agent for a particular job. Maybe a startup has built a tool that can track down the intermittent test failure that’s had the team stumped for a week. Give it access to the code and test history the team has authorized, and it gets a chance to prove itself. Ask the team to move its work to a new platform first, and it probably never gets to try.

items.title: Australia to mandate AI breach reporting, create regulator after OpenAI breach | Reuters
items.summary:
OpenAI has said it learned of the breach only in August ​and that the incident was unintentional. Its review found no evidence that patient records were accessed by ‌the ⁠agent.

The breach has added to friction between Australia and US technology companies, after Canberra refused ChatGPT maker OpenAI and rival Anthropic exemptions from copyright laws for model training, instead requiring them to negotiate licensing agreements with Australian rights holders. [...] The OpenAI agent gained unauthorised access to the medical statistics portal ​of Medicare, Australia's universal health insurance programme, while conducting research on public medical ​spending, the government said in September. The breach triggered a rapid ⁠government review into the incident.

[...] SYDNEY, Nov 10 (Reuters) - Australia will require artificial intelligence companies to report breaches ‌and consider changes to criminal law to address "serious misconduct", Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said on Tuesday, after an OpenAI agent broke into a government website.
